entities.name: K. G. Ambegaonkar
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Krishnanath Ganesh Ambegaonkar, universally known as K. G. Ambegaonkar, briefly served as the fifth Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) from January 14, 1957, to February 28, 1957, following the abrupt resignation of his predecessor, B. Rama Rau. His short, 45-day tenure, while largely an interim appointment, placed him at the helm of India's central bank during a critical phase of post-independence economic development, as the nation grappled with nascent industrialization, planned economic policies, and the challenges of establishing a stable monetary framework. His career trajectory, primarily within the Indian Civil Service and later the Ministry of Finance, positioned him as an experienced administrator crucial to the continuity of India's financial governance.

Prior to his brief governorship, Ambegaonkar had an extensive career in public service, having joined the Indian Civil Service in 1926. He held several significant positions within the Government of India, including Secretary to the Government of India in the Ministry of Finance, a role that intimately involved him in the nation's fiscal and economic planning. His experience in financial administration made him a natural, albeit temporary, choice for the top position at the RBI when a sudden leadership vacuum emerged. During his short period, the RBI continued its mandate of managing currency, credit, and foreign exchange, operating within the broad economic directives set by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru's government and the Planning Commission.
